src: APPSC Assistant Architectural Surveyor & Deputy Surveyor Gen
s: As per AP Reorganization Act, 2014, Government of India shall examine the feasibility of establishing Vizag - Chennai industrial corridor on the lines of
x: The Thirteenth Schedule of the AP Reorganisation Act asks GoI to examine a Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor 'along the lines of the Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor'. The Delhi-Kolkata, Delhi-Raipur and Mumbai-Kolkata corridors are not mentioned.

src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
s: ____ is one of the key initiatives undertaken by the residual state of Andhra Pradesh which is believed to attract investment of close to $17 billion, and will create 20,000 jobs.
o: Construction of Amaravati as State Capital
x: The key names the Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor, the residual State's flagship industrial initiative (ADB-backed, about 800 km). Amaravati, Polavaram and housing are capital, irrigation and welfare projects, not investment-and-jobs corridors. The $17 billion / 20,000 jobs figure itself could not be traced.

src: APPSC Group-II Mains 2019 Paper-3
s: The Vizag-Chennai Industrial Corridor (VCIC) is a key part of
o: ASEAN - The Association of Southeast Asian Nations
Nine districts of the state of Andhra Pradesh
x: VCIC is the first phase of the East Coast Economic Corridor, a gateway to ASEAN markets under Act East, and it traverses nine districts of AP, so 'All of these' is correct.

src: APPSC Divisional Accounts Officer (Mains) General Studies &
s: India's first Coastal Economic Corridor traverses through how many districts of Andhra Pradesh?
x: The VCIC, first phase of India's first coastal economic corridor (ECEC), traverses nine of AP's (then 13) districts.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
s: How may potential industrial nodes are identified on Visakhpatnam-Chennai Industrial Corridor?
x: ADB's plan identified four VCIC nodes: Visakhapatnam, Kakinada, Gannavaram-Kankipadu and Srikalahasti-Yerpedu (nine clusters in all). Today three nodes are being developed (Vizag, Chittoor, Kopparthy).

src: APPSC Sample Taker 2023
s: What is the full form of APIIC in context with the Andhra Pradesh state?
x: APIIC stands for Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation; it is a corporation, not a 'company', and not 'inclusive' or 'independent'.

src: APPSC Group-IV Paper-I Mains 2023
s: What is the expansion of APIIC?
x: APIIC = Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation; the other expansions are invented.

src: APPSC Polytechnic Colleges Lecturers (Engineering & Non-Engi
s: In which year was the Andhra Pradesh Industrial Infrastructure Corporation Ltd. (APIIC) incorporated?
x: APIIC was incorporated in 1973 (26 September 1973).

src: AP recruitment paper (header page missing in scan)
s:
Match the items in
List-I (Places/Projects) with those in
List-II (Location/Details).

A. Krishnapatnam Industrial Area (KRIS City)

B. Sri Venkateswara Mobile and Electronics Hub

C. Sri Kodandarama Temple 'Maha Samprokshanam'

D. Araku Valley

1. Tirupati District, Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor

2. Tirupati, Andhra Pradesh

3. Vontimitta, Kadapa District

4. Alluri Sitharama Raju District
x: Krishnapatnam Industrial Area (KRIS City) is the CBIC node in Tirupati district; the Mobile and Electronics Hub is at Tirupati; the Kodandarama temple is at Vontimitta (Kadapa); Araku is in Alluri Sitharama Raju district: A-1, B-2, C-3, D-4.

src: APPSC Group-II Prelims 2024 (25-02-2024)
s:
Match the following on industrial clusters developed by APIIC Ltd. in Andhra Pradesh:
List I (Location of Industrial Cluster)

a. Gandrajupalle in Chittoor region

b. Kopparthi in Kadapa region

c. Makavarapalem at Visakhapatnam

d. Machilipatnam
List II (Type of Industry)

I. Silk and Garments

II. Engineering

III. Aluminium

IV. Jewellery
x: Machilipatnam is the imitation-jewellery cluster and Makavarapalem the alumina-aluminium park (d-IV, c-III); Gandrajupalle is silk and garments and Kopparthi engineering, which gives option 1.

src: APPSC Group-III Panchayat Secretary Mains Paper-I General St
s: Which of the following is not a potential industrial node under Chennai Bangalore industrial Corridor?
x: The CBIC nodes master-planned with JICA are Ponneri (Tamil Nadu), Tumakuru (Karnataka) and Krishnapatnam (AP). Kuppam is only a town along the route, not a node.

src: APPSC Group-II Prelims 2019 (05-05-2019)
s: How many nodes were taken up for master planning under Japan International Cooperation Agency assistance for Chennai-Bengaluru Industrial Corridor?
x: JICA prepared the Comprehensive Integrated Master Plan for CBIC and master-planned three nodes: Ponneri (Tamil Nadu), Tumakuru (Karnataka) and Krishnapatnam (AP). 'Five nodes' is not supported (printed key: Five).

src: APPSC Group-2 PYQ
s: In the Union Budget 2024-25, the GOI has promised funds to which industrial nodes as part of the Vishakhapatnam-Chennai and Bangalore- Hyderabad industrial corridors?
x: Budget 2024-25 promised funds for the Kopparthi node (Vizag-Chennai corridor) and the Orvakal node (Hyderabad-Bengaluru corridor); the CCEA approved both on 28 Aug 2024. Donakonda is only a long-term VCIC node.

src: State PSC
s: Which one of the following industrial/economic corridors of India is being developed in collaboration with Japan?
x: The Delhi-Mumbai Industrial Corridor is being developed with Japan (MoU 2006); VCIC is ADB-funded. CBIC also has JICA support but is not an option here.

src: APPSC General Studies & Mental Ability (Common Paper for Var
s: Bharatmala Pariyojana Project is related to
x: Bharatmala Pariyojana is the national highways (road connectivity) programme; the Bengaluru-Chennai Expressway is a Bharatmala Phase-I project.

src: APPSC 2021 Mains Junior Assistant Cum Computer Assistant In
s: Construction of Four lane highway in Andhra Pradesh was announced by Minister of Road Transport and Highways Nitin Gadkari in December 2022. Which two places does it connect?
x: On 1 December 2022 Nitin Gadkari announced approval for four-laning NH-716 from Kadapa towards Renigunta (Kadapa-Chinna Orampadu, Rs 1,732.66 crore), cutting Kadapa-Renigunta travel time.

src: APPSC Extension Officer Grade-I Common Paper General Studies
s: As per the Act, the duration of special status to Andhra Pradesh will be for
x:
Most keys: five years 'as per the Act'. Strictly: SCS is not in the AP Reorganisation Act, 2014; the five years come from the PM's Rajya Sabha assurance of 20 Feb 2014.
Five years – the period PM Manmohan Singh promised in the Rajya Sabha on 20 February 2014. The Act itself contains no SCS clause.

src: APPSC Junior Lecturers General Studies & Mental Ability 2020
s: Quoting the issue of revenue deficit after the bifurcation of Andhra Pradesh, what major demand did the then Chief Minister Chandrababu Naidu place before the Government of India?
o: To declare President's rule in the state of Andhra Pradesh
To permanently keep Hyderabad as the common capital for both the states of Andhra Pradesh as well as Telangana
To grant special category status to the state of Andhra Pradesh
To reverse the decision and combine the states of Andhra Pradesh and Telangana again
x: Citing the post-bifurcation revenue deficit, Chandrababu Naidu's main demand was Special Category Status for AP; he never sought President's rule, a permanent common capital or re-merger.

src: APPSC Assistant Social, BC & Tribal Welfare Officers Mains P
s: In February, 2014, where did the then Prime Minister Manmohan Singh announced that Special Category Status would be extended to the State of Andhra Pradesh for five years?
o: In joint sitting of both houses
He did not make any such announcement
x: On 20 February 2014 PM Manmohan Singh announced SCS for AP for five years in the Rajya Sabha; the 2018 no-confidence motion was in the Lok Sabha.

src: Sub Inspectors Paper-IV 2019
s: Who proposed the Multi Dimensional Index (MDI), so as to measure the economic progress of states in India?
x: The Raghuram Rajan Committee (2013) proposed a Multi-Dimensional (composite development) Index of state backwardness; states scoring 0.6 and above were to be 'least developed'.

src: APPSC Polytechnic Lecturers (S2) 2020
s: The recommendation of the 14th Finance Commission regarding increase of the state's share to be increased from 32% to 42% was implemented from which fiscal year?
x: The 14th FC award (2015-20), accepted on 24 Feb 2015, raised the States' share from 32% to 42% from 2015-16.

src: APPSC Group-I 2017
s: What is the amount of special assistance provided by the Central Government to Andhra Pradesh in 2016-17?
x: The Finance Ministry (19 Aug 2016) gave AP special assistance of Rs 1,976.50 crore for 2016-17: Rs 1,176.50 crore resource gap + Rs 350 crore backward districts + Rs 450 crore capital. Rs 1,176.50 crore is only one part, and Rs 4,058.04 crore was wrongly given in the old notes.

src: APPSC Asst. Director in AP Economic & Statistics 2017
s: As per the special package offered by Centre to AP?
o: All loans of Andhra Pradesh would be taken over by Centre
Centre would give matching grant for loans raised by Andhra Pradesh State
Centre would meet entire cost of new capital as per plans of Andhra Pradesh
All loans under Externally Aided projects to Andhra Pradesh would be repaid by Centre
x: Under the special package the Centre repays the loan and interest of externally aided projects signed and disbursed in 2015-16 to 2019-20, up to the SCS-equivalent 90% share. It did not take over all AP loans, give matching grants or fund the whole capital.
